data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F climate and energy technology company founded by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher, has raised over $1.0B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression methodology was applied, using the $1.0B total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F advancement. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $1.3B. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy peer set—while 8 same-sector peers were identified, none met the threshold of 3+ datapoints when filtered by stage, timing, and valuation tier.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B to $1.5B, with a median of $1.3B. This range reflects reliance on a single applicable methodology rather than consensus across multiple independent approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of robust same-stage peer data for direct valuation anchoring and the difficulty in isolating transaction comparables within this emerging sector. Refinement of this range would benefit from additional Series F or late-stage financing data in climate tech.
